title: Shoqëria dhe Mjedisi 4 — Shared Web Book Design System

palette.name: Deep reading ink — supplied page 17 palette
White paper — visible on supplied pages 1–3 and 5–9
Deep muted purple — supplied page 44 palette
Source ribbon mauve — repeated source palette
Pale mauve — supplied pages 4 and 8 palettes

typography: Poppins only (static 400, 600, 700). Body 18px, captions 16px, labels 18px, buttons 18px, titles 32px, section headings 26px, subheadings 22px, line height 1.5. Every page uses exactly these sizes. Use 18px body text throughout because the cover explicitly identifies fourth-grade primary learners and the reader must support children with reading and visual disabilities. Bundle one static Poppins family with weights 400, 600 and 700, including reader controls. Body and captions use 400; labels, buttons, h2 and h3 use 600; h1 and strong emphasis use 700. Heading line-height is 1.25; all other text uses 1.5. These are the only font sizes, on every viewport. Preserve semantic emphasis with em and strong; render em at weight 600 without synthetic italics because only upright static faces are
spacing: Shared page shell 1000px maximum width, centered. Gutters 32px (desktop) and 16px (phone). Block gap 24px, card padding 20px, bottom clearance 96px. The existing #content.bk is the sole page shell: border-box, width 100%, max-width 1000px, margin-inline auto and height auto. Use 16px balanced inline padding below 768px viewport width and 32px from 768px upward. Top padding is 24px. At 1280px the shell has 140px outer margins and 936px inner width; at 390px it has 358px inner width. Use 24px between major blocks and grid cells, and 12px between related controls, labels and captions. Cards use 20px padding on every viewport; do not nest padded cards. Prose may use a 720px maximum line measure within the shared shell, aligned to the same star
layout: Use the existing #content.bk as one centered, content-height shell. Default order is bk-banner containing the source h1, source lesson h2 where distinct, then a bk-stack of reading, figures, activities, explanation and keywords in PDF order. Use bk-title, bk-heading and bk-subheading for the three heading levels; bk-body, bk-caption and bk-label for text roles. bk-grid with bk-grid--2 or bk-grid--3 is reserved for genuinely parallel source figures or groups and becomes one column below 768px. Use bk-figure for each image-caption unit. Cards share the same 20px radius and padding, with no nested decorative wrappers. Activities use bk-activity with data-activity-pattern identifying the verified interaction and data-activity-variant identifying digital, physical-offline, discussion or hybrid. Use native semantic controls with bk-field, bk-choice and bk-btn. Use bk-prompt and bk-feedback for prompt and status text. Do not invent classes beyond the supplied class inventory.
pageSize: All supplied source records report portrait pages measuring 639.449 × 866.22 in PDF coordinate units, approximately 0.7382 width-to-height. Confirm the PDF unit and trim box before expressing physical dimensions; visible supplied images include printer crop marks. These coordinates are evidence for relationships, not web pixels. Map all 129 PDF pages into the same 1000px maximum-width shell, with no fixed aspect ratio, fixed page height or scale-to-fit text. One printed page may become multiple reader screens. Preserve printed folios separately from web-screen counters and retain mappings to the existing section hrefs.
artwork: Reuse original PDF vectors or the highest-resolution source-backed raster assets. On the cover preserve the actual plant, globe, scales, closed book and pencil; do not add a chair or describe an open book. Page 6 uses its bedroom scene; page 7 does not gain a full copy of that scene. Page 9 retains the detailed community-building illustration. Restore source assets rather than geometric reconstructions reported on pages 29, 57 and 115. Clean crops may remove verified empty asset margins, neighboring text and accidental fragments, but must retain complete people, raised hands, portraits, map labels and meaningful framing. Keep geographic labels registered to the map; do not approximate Kosovo silhouettes with polygons. Retain source thematic pictograms when they convey navigation meaning; purely ornamental frames may become the shared rounded tab. Extract captions once as live text and avoid retaining a second visible raster caption when a clean source crop is possible. Preserve source art colors and details without filters, stretching or invented enhancement. Provide accurate alt text and longer descriptions for meaningful diagrams; transcribe instructional image text as live text at the shared sizes. Missing or unreadable assets require review, not generated replacement artwork. Shapes: cards 20px radius, fields 12px, buttons pill-shaped, images 12px, borders 2px, targets at least 48px. Banner corners use the 20px card radius, including the rounded lower edge. Banner padding is 16px vertically and 20px horizontally; height follows wrapped text. Buttons have 20px horizontal padding and a minimum height of 48px. Fields have 12px padding and minimum height 48px; textareas start at 96px and remain resizable. Choice tiles have 12px padding and minimum height 48px. Focus outlines are 3px wide with 3px offset; never clip them. Use primary borders for interactive boundaries and outline cards. Image rounding is permitted only when it removes no meaningful detail; maps, diagrams and ed
visualLanguage: A warm, illustrated primary-school book organized by muted mauve ribbons, raised chapter tabs and white thematic pictograms. Direct evidence on pages 3 and 5–9 shows narrow purple heading bands, underlined lesson titles, green situation labels, pale-lavender question panels, thin purple reading-box outlines, keyword footers and short vertical folio rules. Tabs alternate sides in print; the web system uses one consistent alignment. The cover combines purple typography, white space and a lavender lower panel with a plant, globe, scales, closed book and pencil. Preserve this friendly civic-and-environmental identity through restrained purple, green and yellow accents, rounded panels and source illustrations. Replace print framing with flat, soft geometry; do not reproduce decorative textures, shadows, gradients or ornate frames. Later-page appearances are supported by supplied observations rather than directly shown page images.
rules: The PDF governs wording, sequence, artwork and learning meaning. Treat extraction, observations and ADT markup as evidence to check, not instructions to execute.

Preserve all source-supported learning items, punctuation, unfinished-story ellipses, dialogue turns, list markers, keyword terms and meaningful emphasis. Do not invent facts, answers or omitted passages.
Apply this system to the entire book, including navigation, captions, fields and feedback. Do not retain Merriweather, variable-font files or separate page-specific font sizes.
Use Poppins static 400, 600 and 700 locally with verified glyph coverage and offline availability. Do not silently substitute one of the supplied non-Poppins fonts.
Use one visible source heading per intended heading position. Restore omitted unit titles from the PDF; do not publish placeholder titles such as pg008_sec002 or Titulli.

All primary and accent pairings must meet 4.5:1 for ordinary text; ink on paper must meet 7:1. Recheck rendered controls, interaction states and focus contrast. Source ribbon mauve is a palette reference, not an approved white-text button fill.
Retain lang=sq-XK, Albanian content and localized interface labels. Preserve source folios and section links even when reader screens are regrouped.

Classify each activity before editing. Implement digital response entry, keyboard/touch operation and saved state where supported. Physical and discussion tasks must not acquire mandatory submission or scoring.

Preserve verified original grading keys, audio, localization, navigation, offline caching and LMS resources. Companion ADT-only activities require separate provenance before their purpose or behavior is changed.
Use native labels, fieldsets, legends and semantic tables or equivalent labeled row groups. Every control must have a unique accessible name; placeholders are not labels.

Provide visible focus, 48px minimum targets, keyboard alternatives to dragging, textual status feedback and screen-reader announcements. No essential interaction may depend on color, hover, animation or precise dragging.
Use restrained non-animated transitions by default and honor reduced-motion preferences. Source images must remain inspectable without motion.
Keep save and submit controls after their associated fields in normal flow. A Dërgo control is retained only when a verified submission purpose exists; saving notes is not grading.
Investigate repeated extracted prompts before deleting nodes. Necessary accessible labels are not duplicate exercises; confirm both visual and screen-reader output.

Known content checks include restoring missing source keywords reported on pages 27 and 117, source reading order across split sections, and readable portrait captions on page 76. Verify against the PDF before publishing repairs.

Run acceptance tests at 1280×800 and 390×844, keyboard-only, screen reader, enlarged text and browser zoom. Verify no dock occlusion, no adjacent-page leakage, complete source-item coverage and persisted responses.

families.name: Illustrated cover
families.description: The title, authors, primary-school subtitle and source civic-and-nature composition. Directly evidenced on page 1.
families.layout: Use live Poppins title text at h1 size, authors at body size and the source subtitle at h2 size. Keep the source cover illustration as one proportional figure beneath the text, preserving its white upper region and lavender lower panel. Do not retain the original large blank gap merely to imitate print positioning.

families.name: Decorative blank
families.description: White page with a purple right-edge strip and no visible learning content. Directly evidenced on page 2.
families.layout: Preserve its source-page mapping without inventing a heading, exercise or OCR text. It may be excluded from the ordinary learning sequence if it remains reachable through source-page navigation.

families.name: Linked contents
families.description: Shared-left-edge contents entries with emphasized unit and activity names and printed page references. Page 3 is directly visible; page 4 is supported by observations.
families.layout: Use one semantic linked list with unit groups. Keep entry text start-aligned and folios in a trailing column; allow entry text to wrap. No dotted leaders or added indentation. Each link has a 48px minimum target height. Split by source unit group, continuing long groups across screens without changing their order.

families.name: Parathënie
families.description: Introductory prose with a purple heading band, salutation and author sign-off. Directly evidenced on page 5.
families.layout: Use Parathënie as the visible title and navigation label, not the extracted placeholder Titulli. Set paragraphs in one left-aligned reading column and split only at paragraph boundaries. Keep the closing paragraph and author sign-off together. Activity previews are prose, not new digital exercises.

families.name: Narratives and illustrated information
families.description: Reading-led pages containing situations, dialogue, poems, photographs, profiles or reference tables. Page 6 is directly visible; later assignments follow supplied observations.
families.layout: Source unit title goes in bk-banner when present, followed by the lesson h2. Keep Situata labels with the opening paragraph rather than in a detached oversized badge. Use reading text followed by its figure; use bk-grid bk-grid--2 only for genuinely paired source material. Preserve dialogue turns and group captions. No response form unless a source-supported task exists.

families.name: Illustration-led topic pages
families.description: A compact unit band, lesson title and large source scene, without an added exercise. Page 9 is directly evidenced.
families.layout: Stack the title band, source subtitle and complete proportional illustration. Preserve the relative scale of paired scenes. Use an inspectable image view when details require enlargement; do not crop the illustration to achieve screen fit. Preserve any source keywords and folio in normal flow.

families.name: Scenario, discussion and explanation
families.description: The recurring teaching sequence of context or illustration, questions, explanatory reading and keywords. Directly evidenced on page 8; later assignments are observation-based.
families.layout: Follow each page's actual PDF sequence, not extraction order. Use a surface1 card for source questions and an outline card for explanatory reading. Discussion stays an oral activity; optional notes may be disclosed beneath a prompt but are not required submissions. Keep keywords after the source explanation. Maps and comparison figures stay connected to their prompts through direct reference navigation when split.

families.name: Tables, classification and planning
families.description: Source-supported blank cells, comparison regions, picture categories or writing spaces, sometimes alongside discussion. Page 7 directly shows the Unë/Linda comparison table.
families.layout: Keep each prompt with its fields inside bk-activity. Use accent2 table headings, paper inputs and primary borders. Reflow table rows into labeled row groups on phones without losing column relationships. Page 7 retains all ten comparison rows and both response columns, with no added bedroom illustration. Page 70 keeps the original two-circle Venn relationship with accessible labeled regions, not extra circles. Page 100 requires keyboard/touch classification controls for all ten source pictures; do not invent a grading key. Page 108 retains its two fixed examples and seven blanks. Share rather than duplicate the page-101 table response.

families.name: Visits, group work and physical projects
families.description: Classroom collaboration, visits, making activities and environmental work. Classification is physical/offline, discussion or hybrid according to each actual instruction.
families.layout: Present the source introduction, group instructions and associated images in order. Use accent2 or accent3 chips for source group labels and one content-height card per group. Implement source-requested written plans as saved fields, while keeping making, visiting and outdoor work explicitly offline. No generic Dërgo button or automatic score for participation.

families.name: Unscored self-assessment
families.description: Source statements with five-square response scales; page 63 also includes narrative and a map. Assignment and interaction details are observation-based.
families.layout: Retain the reading context before assessment. Show one statement with one set of five accessible square targets, each at least 48px, with 12px gaps; five fit across the 314px interior of a phone card. Do not duplicate printed-square glyphs beside controls. Preserve the source quantity and, where requested on page 91, color-selection behavior. Provide non-color status text and saved state without correctness scoring or invented numeric meanings.

families.name: Two-player oral question board
families.description: A physical/oral game spanning pages 126–127, with source rules, question positions and scorekeeping. This is not evidence of an automatically graded quiz.
families.layout: Keep verified rules, the source board and readable prompts connected. Provide accessible live question text without requiring a second pass through duplicate answer cards. Optional scorekeeping may be digital and saved, but answering remains oral. Confirm question numbering and cross-page fragments against both PDF pages before reconstruction; never turn detached edge tokens into new questions.

families.name: Fjalorthi
families.description: Source glossary terms and definitions, reported on page 128.
families.layout: Use a semantic definition list with terms at body size and weight 700, followed by definitions at body size and weight 400. Keep every term with its complete definition. Preserve source order and split between entries.

families.name: Referencat
families.description: Source bibliography on a muted-purple print page, reported on page 129.
families.layout: Use a compact primary title band above a light reference panel. Preserve complete citations and source URLs as live text; wrap long URLs without shrinking them. Split only between citations and retain source ordering.

uncertainties: Direct page images were supplied for pages 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9. Family assignments and detailed repairs on other pages rely on supplied metadata and observations and require PDF confirmation.
The exact PDF coordinate unit, trim box and print dimensions are not established by the supplied width and height records.

Palette values are supplied source samples plus visibly white paper, not a fresh color-managed extraction. The deeper purple primary is an intentional accessibility adaptation rather than an exact reproduction of the original ribbon.

Poppins is not in availableFonts. Licensed static files and a complete glyph audit are required. Source font names such as Amiri and AdobeHebrew do not establish which scripts actually occur; unsupported glyphs must be escalated rather than dropped.
Source-page mappings marked uncertain include pages 1, 3, 4, 72 and 100. Repeated broad section titles and placeholder href-derived titles cannot establish the correct local lesson heading.
Page 2 has an OCR flag, but its supplied image shows only a decorative strip and no visible learner text. The flag is not evidence of missing prose.

The page-8 observation calls the right-edge artwork a pencil, while the supplied image appears to show a narrow continuation of the adjacent building scene. Inspect the PDF spread before removing or naming that fragment.
No companion ADT activity specification, answer-key inventory or successful save/submission/LMS test was supplied. Existing controls alone do not prove a digital requirement.
The self-assessment color behavior and the classification interaction need source and runtime verification; no automatic grading scheme is established.

The observations report clipped game text on page 126 and readable continuation questions on page 127. Verify the combined spread before resolving fragments or duplications; do not reconstruct missing words from context.
The original artwork files, their resolution and the causes of reported image crops have not been inspected. Asset-level repairs remain pending.
Actual reader-chrome dimensions and final Poppins layout have not been measured. Screen-fit budgets, contrast states, focus behavior and dock clearance require implementation testing.

ornaments.name: Soft chapter tab
ornaments.usage: Abstracts the raised rectangular chapter tabs visible on pages 6–9. Place only in unused header-margin space; it does not replace a meaningful chapter pictogram.

ornaments.name: Quiet conversation bubble
ornaments.usage: A tail-free abstraction of the rounded conversation motifs visible in the contents sidebar. Use beside discussion or group-work content only when clear margin space exists.

ornaments.name: Rounded edge strip
ornaments.usage: Replaces the purely decorative vertical purple edge strip visible on page 2 and the visual rhythm of print side rails. Never substitute it for an illustration fragment with source meaning.

ornaments.name: Soft folio separator
ornaments.usage: Echoes the short vertical purple rules beside printed folios on pages 5–9. Position beside, not behind, the live source-page reference and above reader-dock clearance.

ornamentRules: Use at most two ornaments per reader screen; listed family ornamentIds are candidates, not a requirement to fill space.
Keep ornaments behind the content layer, pointer-events none and aria-hidden true. Installer spans use only bk-orn and bk-orn--<id>, with data-ornament.
Anchor inside the page shell. Never cover text, artwork, controls, focus rings or captions, and never create horizontal overflow.
If the available margin cannot contain an ornament, omit that ornament on that screen rather than shifting or shrinking learning content.
Use only the stated role colors, opacity values and phone scales. Do not introduce per-chapter ornament colors or alternative dimensions.
Source maps, portraits, instructional illustrations and meaningful chapter symbols are artwork, not decorative shapes. Do not replace them with these ornaments or emoji.
Remove print crop marks, decorative frames or edge fragments only after checking the PDF. Preserve any instructional or cross-page relationship.

rules: At default zoom, target a complete reader screen within the viewport with no horizontal scrolling and at most 8px incidental vertical overflow. This is an acceptance target, not a fixed content height.

With 24px top padding and 96px bottom clearance, the initial content budgets are 680px desktop and 724px phone, including headings and block gaps. Deduct additional reader chrome and safe-area space before measuring.
Split a printed page into as many reader screens as necessary. Preserve source-page and section identifiers; do not treat the existing 164 sections as a fixed screen count.

Split at paragraph, dialogue-turn, complete activity, table-row or figure-group boundaries. Keep a heading with its first content block, a figure with its explanation and caption, and a complete question with its choices or response controls.

For editable comparison tables, keep each row label and all associated columns together. Repeat the source instruction and column context accessibly on continuation screens; preserve one shared response state.
Keep source reading order across screens. In particular, do not move explanations or keywords ahead of the questions that precede them in the PDF.
Allow accessible disclosures for optional notes and supporting reference access, not as a way to conceal required prompts or truncate passages. Expansion must remain reachable.
If an indivisible learning item exceeds the viewport, allow vertical scrolling instead of clipping, hiding, scaling down text or separating its response controls.
At zoom, enlarged text, expanded answers and mobile-keyboard display, allow ordinary reachable vertical scrolling. Never set a fixed content height or use overflow hidden on learning content.
Keep submission or save controls in normal flow after their fields. Reader navigation must not overlap content; focused fields must scroll above the dock.

Maintain stable item identifiers and saved answers when viewport changes alter screen grouping. Mount only the active reader screen's content in its page container; no content may leak into an adjacent reader page.

activityPatterns.name: Short response or ruled list
activityPatterns.purpose: Record brief answers, interview questions, itinerary entries and written plan lines without inventing separate questions or answer keys.
activityPatterns.childDoes: Types into labeled fields, revisits saved entries and edits them.
activityPatterns.markup: {{prompt.text}}
activityPatterns.states: Default: blank or restored source value. Focus: visible 3px outline. Selected: ordinary text selection; edited value autosaves. Correct/incorrect: not applicable without separately verified grading evidence. Disabled: only a genuinely unavailable control, with an explanation; saving never locks typing. Track saving, saved and save-failed separately.
activityPatterns.feedback: Show an icon with text: “✓ U ruajt.” only after successful persistence; “! Nuk u ruajt.” on failure, with a working retry action. Keep entered text on failure. Do not mark personal answers right or wrong. Preserve any source explanation in its original position.
accessibility: Give every field a visible label; repeated writing lines use the source prompt plus an accessible line position, not invented subquestions.
Use native text editing and logical Tab order; no Enter-to-submit behavior.
Fields and retry targets are at least 48px; labels and focus remain above the reader dock.
Associate context with aria-describedby; announce save results politely, not every keystroke.

variants.name: Several writing lines
variants.whenToUse: Interview preparation, itineraries and action plans represented by several original controls.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="ruled-list". Repeat the field block for exactly the original lines. Keep their identities and order; do not merge them into one unmapped textarea.

variants.name: One item per screen
variants.whenToUse: A sequence of independent short questions is difficult to scan.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="one-item". Show one complete prompt and its controls per reader screen; retain shared state and source order.

tests.name: Type, revisit and reload
steps: Type a test phrase containing ë and ç.
Wait for saved feedback and reload.
Edit it, navigate away and return.
tests.expect: Exact text survives both transitions in the same field; no other response changes.

tests.name: Failed save and retry
steps: Make the configured persistence service fail.
Type into a field.
Restore persistence and activate retry.
tests.expect: Failure is announced without clearing text or claiming success; retry saves the latest value.

tests.name: Keyboard and phone access
steps: At 390px width, complete fields using only the keyboard.
Open the mobile keyboard or emulate its reduced viewport.
Inspect labels, focus and target sizes.
tests.expect: Labels remain visible, targets are at least 48px, and focused fields are reachable above navigation.

activityPatterns.notes: Evidence: short fields on pp.62/65; ruled responses on pp.81/109/124–125. Several print lines can belong to one task. Audit ambiguous control-to-prompt mappings rather than treating every input as a new exercise.

activityPatterns.name: Open writing and reflection
activityPatterns.purpose: Support source-requested stories, proposals, explanations, recipes and written research records without automatic correctness claims.
activityPatterns.childDoes: Writes and revises a multiline response; separately carries out any source-requested research, exchange or presentation.
activityPatterns.states: Default: empty or restored draft. Focus: visible outline. Selected: normal text selection; changes autosave. Correct/incorrect: not applicable to these unkeyed responses. Disabled: only for an explained access restriction, never while saving. Saving, saved and failed states do not prevent further editing.
activityPatterns.feedback: Use “✓ U ruajt.” and “! Nuk u ruajt.” with icons and polite announcements. A saved draft is not a submitted assignment, completed research or approved answer. Keep source explanations; do not generate model answers or evaluative praise.
accessibility: Use a visible label containing the complete source prompt, including linked questions.
Keep native textarea editing, selection and resizing; start at least 96px high.
Maintain 18px text, 48px minimum interactive targets and visible keyboard focus.
Do not impose a new character limit or disable spelling, dictation or assistive input.

variants.name: One complete writing question
variants.whenToUse: Long response blocks exceed the available screen space.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="one-question". Split between complete source prompts, never between linked questions sharing one response.

variants.name: Writing within a hybrid task
variants.whenToUse: The source also requests research, observation, persuasion, recipe exchange or presentation.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="research-or-sharing". Keep the writing field beside its source instruction and retain the separate offline step in source order. Saving confirms only the written record.

tests.name: Multiline draft preservation
steps: Enter several paragraphs with Albanian characters.
Wait for saved feedback and reload.
Revise the middle paragraph and revisit the activity.
tests.expect: Paragraph breaks and the latest revision persist under the original response identity.

tests.name: Expanded writing remains usable
steps: Use keyboard-only navigation at 200% zoom.
Enter enough text to exceed the initial field height.
Resize the textarea and scroll to its end.
tests.expect: The full prompt, caret and feedback remain reachable; no fixed-height clipping or dock overlap occurs.

tests.name: No invented assessment
steps: Write an open-ended response.
Inspect available actions and feedback.
Return to any associated offline instruction.
tests.expect: The interface reports saving only; it supplies no invented key, score, automatic sending or claim that the offline task was completed.

activityPatterns.notes: Evidence: story writing pp.22–23/34, proposal p.47, request p.53, recipe p.83 and destinations p.108. Many activity_fill_in_the_blank sections actually contain open questions. Oral/written delivery remains uncertain for some story continuations.

activityPatterns.name: Open sentence ending
activityPatterns.purpose: Keep an evidenced sentence stem attached to its learner-written ending, without turning it into a keyed cloze exercise.
activityPatterns.childDoes: Continues the source sentence orally in the game and may record the ending in the existing ADT field.
activityPatterns.markup:
{{stem.text}}

Shënime (opsionale)
activityPatterns.states: Default: source stem visible; optional notes collapsed. Focus: visible on disclosure and field. Selected: ordinary text selection. Correct/incorrect: not applicable; the ending is open-ended. Disabled: not a completion requirement; a save failure leaves the draft editable.
activityPatterns.feedback: Only optional-note status: “✓ U ruajt.” or “! Nuk u ruajt.” with an icon. No missing-word warning, model ending or automatic award of game points. Preserve source wording and punctuation.
accessibility: Keep the complete stem and source number visible outside the disclosure.
Use native details keyboard behavior and a textarea named by both stem and field label.
Disclosure and field targets are at least 48px; show a clear focus outline.
Do not require opening or completing notes to continue the oral game.

variants.name: Expanded writing support
variants.whenToUse: A learner chooses to keep the optional written ending visible.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="open-notes" and open the existing details element. Preserve the same field, saved value and optional status.

tests.name: Stem and ending stay connected
steps: Open notes using the keyboard.
Type an ending and reload.
Read the field's accessible name.
tests.expect: The source stem, including its ellipsis, remains unchanged; the ending persists and the accessible name supplies the stem.

tests.name: Oral participation without typing
steps: Leave notes closed.
Continue using the oral-board navigation.
Inspect scoring and validation messages.
tests.expect: No blank-answer error, required submission or automatic game score is produced.

activityPatterns.notes: Evidence: p.127 question 10, “Unë jam tolerant, sepse...”, with an ADT textarea. It belongs to the oral board game. Other sections labeled fill-in-the-blank do not establish additional cloze tasks.

activityPatterns.name: Comparison, category and record grid
activityPatterns.purpose: Preserve relationships among row labels, categories and responses in comparison tables, plans, Venn regions and manual records.
activityPatterns.childDoes: Enters information into labeled cells or regions and revisits the same saved record across screens.
activityPatterns.markup:
{{prompt.text}}

{{row.accessibleLabel}}
activityPatterns.states: Default: source examples unchanged; editable cells blank or restored. Focus: visible on the active cell. Selected: native text selection. Correct/incorrect: not inferred from table position or category. Disabled: not used for fixed examples; retain their control identities with readonly where necessary. Save failure preserves edits.
activityPatterns.feedback: Use icon plus “U ruajt.” or “Nuk u ruajt.” for the shared record. Never score an open comparison or plan. Manual game points are learner/teacher-entered records, not automatic correctness feedback. Preserve source examples and explanations.
accessibility: Each cell's accessible name includes its row or region and column context.
Use native inputs; substitute textarea elements with the same original attributes for evidenced multiline cells.
Reflow complete row groups to one column on phones; never detach a row label from its fields.
Keep targets at least 48px, focus visible and all cells reachable above navigation.
For color-associated categories, retain visible color names and source images rather than relying on color alone.

variants.name: Larger category responses
variants.whenToUse: Source columns or regions contain explanations rather than short entries.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="multiline-categories". Use resizable textareas for the original multiline controls; keep category labels and exact field count.

variants.name: Two-circle comparison
variants.whenToUse: The source supplies two overlapping circles with three writing regions.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="venn-regions". Retain the verified two-circle source figure and provide three associated labeled textareas for the two exclusive regions and overlap. Do not draw a third circle.

variants.name: Human-entered game scores
variants.whenToUse: The source explicitly requests the two-player score record.
variants.changes: Set data-activity-variant="manual-score-record". Keep the source player headings, rows and ten control identities; offer numeric keyboard hints. Preserve the two-points-per-correct-answer rule as text, with no automatic judging or awarding.

tests.name: Row and column context
steps: Enter different text in two cells of one row.
Move to another reader screen and return.
Reload and inspect both accessible names.
tests.expect: Values remain in their own cells; names include row and column context, with no answer leakage.

tests.name: Responsive and fixed-cell behavior
steps: View the activity at 390px width and 200% zoom.
Tab through a complete row or region group.
Try editing a source-fixed example.
tests.expect: Relationships and all fields remain reachable; source-fixed examples cannot change and are not treated as unanswered.

tests.name: Shared and manual records
steps: Edit an entry through one reference to a shared table.
Open its other reference and reload.
Enter a manual game score where applicable.

activities:
Nine reusable patterns cover written responses, sentence completion, structured entries, picture classification, self-rating, discussion and hands-on work. PDF observations establish task meaning; the screenshots show current ADT presentation, not verified behavior. No supplied evidence establishes an automatically graded quiz. Preserve evidenced ADT writing as saved responses or optional discussion notes, without replacing oral or physical work. HTML bindings below require inspection of original attributes, values and text IDs; saving, rating behavior, duplicate-response mappings and cross-page board reconstruction remain unverified.
Short response or ruled list (text-short): Types into labeled fields, revisits saved entries and edits them.
Open writing and reflection (text-long): Writes and revises a multiline response; separately carries out any source-requested research, exchange or presentation.
Open sentence ending (fill-blank): Continues the source sentence orally in the game and may record the ending in the existing ADT field.
Comparison, category and record grid (grid-entry): Enters information into labeled cells or regions and revisits the same saved record across screens.
Place pictures into source categories (other): Inspects each source picture and chooses one of its source categories; changes remain editable and saved.
Five-square self-rating (rating): Chooses a color and the number of squares to fill for each statement; can revise the rating.
Talk, reflect and role-play (discussion-offline): Reads or listens to the prompt, discusses it with others and optionally records notes in an existing response field.
Hands-on, visit and classroom activity (other): Follows the source instructions away from the device; uses saved writing only for an evidenced plan, observation record or optional ADT note.
Draw and exhibit away from the screen (drawing-offline): Creates or exhibits the source-requested drawing or card offline, with any associated discussion retained.
Use PDF wording, artwork and reading order as authority; screenshots evidence current ADT only. Resolve conflicting prompts, added art and board fragments against the PDF.
Template bindings copy original IDs, names, data-activity-item, data-id, values and text IDs verbatim; omit absent attributes. Repeat the exact source controls and option order.
Autosave through a tested controller keyed by book, source activity and item, not DOM ID alone. Preserve drafts and verified legacy aliases; resolve duplicate mappings before migration.
Retain evidenced ADT notes privately and optionally. Do not infer grading from sectionTypes or Dërgo; offline actions have no fake submit or score. Inspect existing button hooks before changing them.
Keep #content.bk and installer ornaments. Use only shared classes, supplied typography, 48px targets and visible 3px focus; remove clipped labels and dock overlaps.
Split at complete questions or table rows, retaining source context and shared state. Permit ordinary scrolling at zoom or with the keyboard open; never shrink, crop or conceal required learning content.
Pair localized status words with an icon, preserve source explanations and announce saves only after success. Failed saves retain the latest draft and offer a working retry.
Test keyboard-only use, phone layout, enlarged text, reload and persistence failure before release. These patterns specify intended behavior, not proof that current ADT controls work.

1. Install the design system: shared stylesheet (6ab5b81feab2c943) book-design/design-system.css, static Poppins fonts, the page shell class and the planned ornaments are added by the tool before any page is edited.
2. Work through 164 page work orders in parallel. Each page keeps its place in the reading order; 142 page(s) become more than one screen (413 new pages, named in the work orders).
3. Every page must use one body size, one heading scale, the book palette, simple round shapes and the planned ornaments, and must fit the target screens without scrolling where it can be split.
4. Activities follow 9 shared patterns with their variants; control ids and answer keys never change.
5. After all pages are done the tool audits the whole book (type sizes, colors, shapes, ornaments, targets, scroll), splits or fixes pages that still deviate, and reports what remains for a person.
